title: Recover exact interrupted record transactions
description: An operator obtains an exact attributable terminal state or a safe recovery stop while retaining enough valid information for subsequent recovery. This logical behavior has the scope and limits of SR-045; current SQLite realization and maintenance remain distinct.
inputs: Explicit supported operation, selected project/Change and expected coherent state.
Actor-supplied candidate or verified recovery basis, with declared subject and artifact identities.
outputs: Exact attributable result or explicit conflict, unavailability, rejection or recovery-required outcome.
behavior: Unavailable, corrupted, unsupported or unrecognized recovery information causes an explicit safe stop; foreign or newer work is not overwritten through guessed repair.

Where explicit completion or restoration is supported, completion reproduces the exact prepared candidate with applicable fresh basis checks and restoration reproduces the verified before-state; neither replays actor operations or edits external basis subjects.
Committed success cannot be rolled back as interruption repair. Recovery of uncommitted creation preserves all preexisting and externally added content.
Interruption during recovery remains attributable and repeatable without duplicate semantic effects; an unverified terminal state is never reported as complete.

Automatic storage recovery may only establish the transaction outcome already determined by the supported storage contract. Ordinary reads never choose completion versus restoration, import history or apply a new actor decision. An unresolved choice requires explicit recovery selection.

failure_behavior.condition: The requested candidate, expected state or recovery basis cannot be established safely.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return the corresponding bounded rejection, conflict or recovery condition without invented decisions, silent merge or unrelated overwrite.
